## Sales Team Architecture

Building a sales team is both an art and a science. The best sales organizations combine the right people, processes and tools into a predictable revenue engine. This guide quotes no salary, quota or ramp benchmarks, because we have not cited a source for any.

### Sales Org Design by Stage

*A rule of thumb for illustration, not a standard.*

| Company stage | Sales team structure |
|---|---|
| Founder-led | Founders selling, perhaps one AE |
| Early sales | A few AEs, with SDR support |
| Growth | A sales leader, team leads, a larger AE team, an SDR team |
| Scale | A CRO, directors, specialized teams, sales ops |
| Enterprise | A global organization with regional leaders and segment teams |

### Compensation by Role

Sales pay combines base and variable pay, and the split changes with the role. Quota multiples and on-target earnings vary by segment, market and company. Benchmark against a current, named compensation source and set quotas from your own history.

### The Sales Hiring Assessment

#### Discovery Call Simulation

Role-play a prospect meeting. Evaluate:

- Question quality and sequencing
- Active listening and note-taking
- Ability to uncover pain and quantify impact
- Poise and professionalism

#### Presentation or Demo

Have them present a product they know well. Evaluate:

- Storytelling ability
- Handling of objections
- Ability to connect features to business value
- Closing technique

#### Pipeline Review

Walk through their current or recent pipeline. Evaluate:

- Pipeline management rigor
- Deal qualification methodology, such as BANT or MEDDPICC
- Forecasting accuracy
- Strategic account planning

#### References

Sales references are important:

- Talk to former managers about consistency, not just peak performance
- Ask about quota attainment over multiple quarters
- Understand the market conditions and territory they operated in

### Factors to Weigh in Sales Hires

These are judgment calls, not measured weights.

| Factor | How to assess |
|---|---|
| Coachability | Give feedback during the interview and see whether they adapt |
| Curiosity | The quality of questions asked during the discovery role-play |
| Work ethic | Activity history from previous roles |
| Intelligence | Ability to understand complex business problems |
| Prior success | Quota attainment, adjusted for territory and market |
| Industry experience | Often teachable, so prioritize selling ability |

### Ramp Time by Role

Ramp time grows with deal complexity: SDRs ramp fastest, SMB AEs next, then mid-market AEs, then enterprise AEs. Measure your own ramp from past hires and plan quotas around it.
